en: || The One Hundred and Eight Names of Śrī Aṣṭalakṣmī || Victory, victory to Śaṅkara! Oṃ, salutations to the Supreme Brahman, the Lord Candramaulīśvara, together with the Supreme Goddess Śrī Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī. Now begins the one hundred and eight names of Śrī Aṣṭalakṣmī: 1. The List of Names of Śrī Ādilakṣmī: Oṃ Śrīṃ. 2. The List of Names of Śrī Dhānyalakṣmī: Oṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ. 3. The List of Names of Śrī Dhairyalakṣmī: Oṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ.

Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ 4: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Gajalakṣmī. Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ 5: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Santānalakṣmī. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ 6: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Vijayalakṣmī. Oṃ klīṃ oṃ 7: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Vidyālakṣmī. Oṃ aiṃ oṃ 8: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Aiśvaryalakṣmī. Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ 1: The *Nāmāvali* of Śrī Ādilakṣmī.

Oṃ Śrīṃ! Salutations to Ādilakṣmī; salutations to Akārā; salutations to Avyayā; salutations to Acyutā; salutations to Ānandā; salutations to Arcitā; salutations to Anugrahā; salutations to Amṛtā; salutations to Anantā; salutations to Iṣṭaprāpti; salutations to Īśvarī; salutations to Kartrī; salutations to Kāntā; salutations to Kalā; salutations to Kalyāṇī; salutations to Kapardinī; salutations to Kamalā; salutations to Kāntivardhinī; salutations to Kumārī; salutations to Kāmākṣī; salutations to Kīrtilakṣmī.

Salutations to Gandhinī; salutations to her who is mounted upon an elephant; salutations to Gambhīravadanā; salutations to Cakrahāsinī; salutations to Cakrā; salutations to Jyotirlakṣmī; salutations to Jayalakṣmī; salutations to Jyeṣṭhā; salutations to Jagajjananī; salutations to Jāgṛtā; salutations to Triguṇā; salutations to Tryailokyamohinī; salutations to Tryailokyapūjitā; salutations to Nānārūpiṇī; salutations to Nikhilā; salutations to Nārāyaṇī; salutations to Padmākṣī; salutations to Paramā; salutations to Prāṇā.

Salutations to Pradhānā; salutations to Prāṇaśakti; salutations to Brahmāṇī; salutations to Bhāgyalakṣmī; salutations to Bhūdevī; salutations to Bahurūpā; salutations to Bhadrakālī; salutations to Bhīmā; salutations to Bhairavī; salutations to Bhogalakṣmī; salutations to Bhūlakṣmī; salutations to Mahāśrī; salutations to Mādhavī; salutations to Mātṛ; salutations to Mahālakṣmī; salutations to Mahāvīrā; salutations to Mahāśakti; salutations to Mālāśrī; salutations to Rājñī; salutations to Ramā.

Salutations to the Fortune of Sovereignty; salutations to the Delightful One; salutations to Lakṣmī; salutations to the Marked One; salutations to the Scribe; salutations to the Fortune of Victory; salutations to the One of Universal Form; salutations to the Refuge of the Universe; salutations to the Large-Eyed One; salutations to the Pervasive One; salutations to the Knower; salutations to the Ocean; salutations to the Tigress; salutations to Vārāhī; salutations to Vaināyakī; salutations to the One of Excellent Limbs; salutations to the Fearless One; salutations to the Auspicious One; salutations to Śākambharī; salutations to the Beloved of Śrī.

Salutations to Kālā; salutations to Śaraṇyā; salutations to Śruti; salutations to Svapnadurgā; salutations to her who has the sun, moon, and fire as her three eyes; salutations to her who rides upon a lion; salutations to Sarvadīpikā; salutations to Sthirā; salutations to her whose form is all prosperity; salutations to Svāminī; salutations to Sitā; salutations to Sūkṣmā; salutations to Sarvasampannā; salutations to Haṃsinī; salutations to Harṣapradā; salutations to Haṃsagā; salutations to Harisūtā; salutations to Harṣaprādhānyā.

Salutations to the Lord of the Greens; salutations to the Mother of All Knowledge; salutations to the Mother of All Beings; salutations to the Bestower of Desired Fruits; salutations to the One of Great Form; salutations to the Performer of Prosperity; salutations to the Auspiciousness; salutations to the One Residing in the Center of the Śrīcakra; salutations to the Creator of Fortune; salutations to Forgiveness. Om. 2. The Garland of Names of Śrī Dhānyalakṣmī.

Oṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, salutations to Dhānyalakṣmī; salutations to Ānandākṛti; salutations to Aninditā; salutations to Ādyā; salutations to Ācāryā; salutations to Abhayā; salutations to Aśakyā; salutations to Ajayā; salutations to Ajeyā; salutations to Amalā; salutations to Amṛtā; salutations to Amarā; salutations to Indrāṇīvaradā; salutations to Indīvareśvarī; salutations to Uragendraśayanā; salutations to Utkelī; salutations to Kāśmīravāsinī; salutations to Kādambaryā; salutations to Kalaravā.

Salutations to her who is adorned with the orb of her breasts; salutations to Kauśikī; salutations to Kṛtamālā; salutations to Kauśāmbī; salutations to Kośavardhinī; salutations to Khaḍgadharā; salutations to Khanī; salutations to Khasthā; salutations to Gītā; salutations to Gītapriyā; salutations to Gīti; salutations to Gāyatrī; salutations to Gautamī; salutations to her who is adorned with variegated ornaments; salutations to Cāṇūrmadinī; salutations to Caṇḍā; salutations to Caṇḍahantrī; salutations to Caṇḍikā; salutations to Gaṇḍakī.

Salutations to Dharmādhārā; salutations to Dhanā; salutations to Dhārā; salutations to Dhanurdharī; salutations to Nābhasā; salutations to Nāsā; salutations to Nūtanāṅgā; salutations to Narakaghnī; salutations to Nuti; salutations to Nāgapāśadharā; salutations to Nityā; salutations to Parvatanandinī; salutations to Pativratā; salutations to Patimayī; salutations to Priyā; salutations to Prītimañjarī; salutations to Pātālavāsinī; salutations to Pūrti; salutations to Pāñcālī; [salutations] to those of living beings.

Salutations to Prasavā; salutations to Parāśakti; salutations to Balimātṛ; salutations to Bṛhaddhāmnī; salutations to she who is praised by Bādarāyaṇa; salutations to Bhayaghnī; salutations to Bhīmarūpā; salutations to Bilvā; salutations to Bhūtasthā; salutations to Makhā; salutations to Mātāmahī; salutations to Mahāmātrī; salutations to Madhyamā; salutations to Mānasī; salutations to Manu; salutations to Menakā; salutations to Mudā; salutations to she who is bound to that supreme state; salutations to Yaśodā; salutations to Yādavā.

Salutations to Yūti; salutations to Raktadantikā; salutations to Ratipriyā; salutations to Ratikarī; salutations to Raktakeśī; salutations to Raṇapriyā; salutations to Laṅkā; salutations to Lavaṇodadhi; salutations to Laṅkeśahaṃtrī; salutations to Lekhā; salutations to Varapradā; salutations to Vāmanā; salutations to Vaidikī; salutations to Vidyut; salutations to Vārāhī; salutations to Suprabhā; salutations to Samidh; Om! 3. Now follows the *Nāmāvali* (litany of names) of Śrī Dhairyalakṣmī.

Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, salutations to Dhairya-lakṣmī; salutations to Apūrvā; salutations to Anādyā; salutations to Adirīśvarī; salutations to Abhīṣṭā; salutations to Ātmarūpiṇī; salutations to Aprameyā; salutations to Aruṇā; salutations to Alakṣyā; salutations to Advaitā; salutations to Ādi-lakṣmī; salutations to Īśāna-varadā; salutations to Indirā; salutations to Unnata-ākārā; salutations to Uddhaṭa-mada-apahā; salutations to Kruddhā; salutations to Kṛśāṅgī; salutations to Kāya-varjitā; salutations to Kāminī.

Salutations to Kuntahastā; salutations to Kulavidyā; salutations to Kaulikī; salutations to Kāvyaśakti; salutations to Kalātmikā; salutations to Khecarī; salutations to Kheṭakāmadā; salutations to Goptrī; salutations to Guṇāḍhyā; salutations to Gavī; salutations to Candrā; salutations to Cārū; salutations to Candraprabhā; salutations to Cañcu; salutations to Caturāśramapūjitā; salutations to Citī; salutations to Gosvarūpā; salutations to Gautamākhyamunistutā; salutations to Gānapriyā.

Salutations to the destroyer of the deceptive Daityas; salutations to Jayā; salutations to Jayantī; salutations to the giver of victory; salutations to her who desires the welfare of the three worlds; salutations to Jātarūpā; salutations to Jyotsnā; salutations to Janatā; salutations to Tārā; salutations to Tripadā; salutations to Tomarā; salutations to Tuṣṭi; salutations to Dhanurdharā; salutations to Dhenukā; salutations to Dhvajinī; salutations to Dhīrā; salutations to the remover of the darkness of dust; salutations to Dhvani; salutations to Dhyeyā.

Salutations to Dhanyā; salutations to Naukā; salutations to her whose splendor is like a dark blue cloud; salutations to Navyā; salutations to Nīlāmbarā; salutations to Nakha-jvālā; salutations to Nalinī; salutations to Parātmikā; salutations to her who destroys the slander of others; salutations to Pannagendra-śayanā; salutations to Patagendra-kṛtāsana; salutations to Pākaśāsanā; salutations to Paraśu-priyā; salutations to Bali-priyā; salutations to Baladā; salutations to Bālikā; salutations to Bālā; salutations to Badarī.

Salutations to the one endowed with strength; salutations to the beloved of Balabhadra; salutations to Intelligence; salutations to the Bāhudā river; salutations to the foremost one; salutations to the giver of liberation; salutations to the one in the form of a fish; salutations to Sacrifice; salutations to the limbs of sacrifice; salutations to the bestower of the fruits of sacrifice; salutations to the embodiment of sacrifice; salutations to the performer of sacrifice; salutations to the delightful one; salutations to the form of Rāma; salutations to the passionate one; salutations to the knower of passion; salutations to the beloved of passion; salutations to the one whose womb contains jewels; salutations to the mine of jewels.

Salutations to Rākṣasī; salutations to Lakṣaṇāḍhyā; salutations to Lolārkaparipūjitā; salutations to Vetravatī; salutations to Viśveśā; salutations to Vīramātā; salutations to Vīraśrī; salutations to Vaiṣṇavī; salutations to Śuci; salutations to Śraddhā; salutations to Śoṇākṣī; salutations to Śeṣavaṃditā; salutations to Śatākṣī; salutations to Hatadānavā; salutations to Hayagrīvatanu. Om. 4. The *Śrīgajalakṣmīnāmāvali*.

Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, salutations to Gajalakṣmī; salutations to Anantaśakti; salutations to Ajñeyā; salutations to Aṇurūpā; salutations to Aruṇākṛti; salutations to Avācyā; salutations to Anantarūpā; salutations to Ambudā; salutations to Ambarasaṃsthāṅkā; salutations to Aśeṣasvarabhūṣitā; salutations to Icchā; salutations to Indīvaraprabhā; salutations to Umā; salutations to Ūrvaśī; salutations to Udayapradā; salutations to Kuśāvartā; salutations to Kāmadhenu; salutations to Kapilā; salutations to Kulodbhavā.

Salutations to her whose body is marked with saffron; salutations to the Virgin; salutations to her who is crimson as saffron; salutations to her who resembles the *kāśa* flower; salutations to the destroyer of the wicked; salutations to the one who moves through the sky; salutations to her whose form is like a bird; salutations to her whose fame is sung by the Gandharvas; salutations to her who is expert in the science of song; salutations to her who has a deep navel; salutations to the embodiment of gravity; salutations to the Chamari deer; salutations to the four-faced one; salutations to her who is worshipped in the sixty-four Śrī Tantras; salutations to the bliss of consciousness; salutations to the one worthy of contemplation.

Salutations to the Profound One; salutations to the One to be Sung; salutations to the One served by Gandharvas; salutations to the Destroyer of Old Age and Death; salutations to the Victorious One; salutations to the One resembling a Cloud; salutations to the Life-Sustainer; salutations to the Bestower of Life; salutations to the One who has Conquered Breath; salutations to the Conqueror of Enemies; salutations to the Mother; salutations to Satiety; salutations to Modesty; salutations to Thirst; salutations to the One worshipped by Dakṣa; salutations to the One with Long Hair; salutations to the Compassionate One; salutations to the Destroyer of Danujas; salutations to the Destroyer of Poverty.

Salutations to Dravā, salutations to Nītiniṣṭhā, salutations to the bestower of the celestial path, salutations to Nāgarūpā, salutations to Nāgavallī, salutations to Pratiṣṭhā, salutations to Pītāmbarā, salutations to Parā, salutations to Puṇyaprajñā, salutations to Payoṣṇī, salutations to Pampā, salutations to Padmapayasvinī, salutations to Pīvarā, salutations to Bhīmā, salutations to the remover of the fear of worldly existence, salutations to Bhīṣmā, salutations to her whose neck is adorned with shining jewels, and salutations to her who is worthy of worship by her brothers.

Salutations to Bhārgavī; salutations to Bhrājiṣṇu; salutations to her whose splendor is equal to ten million suns; salutations to Mātaṅgī; salutations to Mānadā; salutations to Mātṛ; salutations to her who dwells in the circle of Mothers; salutations to Māyā; salutations to Māyāpurī; salutations to Yaśasvinī; salutations to Yogagamyā; salutations to Yogyā; salutations to her who wears jeweled armlets and bracelets; salutations to Rati-rāga-vivardhinī; salutations to Rolamba-pūrṇa-mālā; salutations to Ramaṇīyā; salutations to Ramāpatī; salutations to Lekhyā.

Salutations to Lāvaṇyabhū; salutations to Lipī; salutations to Lakṣmaṇā; salutations to Vedamātṛ; salutations to Vahnisvarūpadhṛṣ; salutations to Vāgurā; salutations to Vadhurūpā; salutations to Vālihaṃtrī; salutations to Varāpsarasī; salutations to Śāmbarī; salutations to Śamanī; salutations to Śānti; salutations to Sundarī; salutations to Sītā; salutations to Subhadrā; salutations to Kṣemaṅkarī; salutations to Kṣiti. Om. 5. The *Śrī Santānalakṣmī Nāmāvali*.

Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, salutation to Santānalakṣmī; salutation to Asuraghnī; salutation to Arcitā; salutation to Amṛtaprasavā; salutation to Akārarūpā; salutation to Ayodhyā; salutation to Aśvinī; salutation to Amaravallabhā; salutation to Akhaṇḍitāyuḥ; salutation to Indunibhānanā; salutation to Ijyā; salutation to Indrādistutā; salutation to Uttamā; salutation to Utkṛṣṭavarṇā; salutation to Urvī; salutation to Kamalasragdharā; salutation to Kāmavaradā; salutation to Kamaṭhākṛti.

Salutations to her who is beautiful with a girdle of bells; salutations to her praised by the one seated on the lotus; salutations to the one born from the *kaṃbū* tree; salutations to the giver of boons to Kautsa; salutations to the dweller in Kāmarūpa; salutations to the wielder of the sword; salutations to her whose form is the qualities; salutations to her exalted by the qualities; salutations to her who has the form of a cowherd; salutations to the protector; salutations to the profound one; salutations to the bestower of wealth in cattle; salutations to her whose nature is consciousness; salutations to the one who moves and is unmoving; salutations to the variegated one; salutations to the wonderful one; salutations to the most venerable one; salutations to the one who is attainable.

Salutations to Godā; salutations to the giver of a son to her guru; salutations to Tāmraparṇī; salutations to the one consisting of sacred fords (tīrthamayī); salutations to Tāpasī; salutations to the beloved of ascetics; salutations to the one worshipped by the three worlds; salutations to the deluder of people; salutations to the one whose form is water; salutations to the seed of the universe; salutations to the Mother; salutations to the destroyer of rebirth; salutations to the sustainer of the world; salutations to the one who has conquered the senses; salutations to the consort of Light; salutations to Draupadī; salutations to the mother of the gods; salutations to the invincible one.

Salutations to the Bestower of Radiance; salutations to the Destroyer of the Ten-Faced One; salutations to the Swinging One; salutations to Splendor; salutations to the Radiant One; salutations to the Praised One; salutations to the Slayer of Niṣumbha; salutations to Narmadā; salutations to She Who is Named by the Stars; salutations to Nandinī; salutations to Padminī; salutations to Her Whose Eyes are Like Lotus Calyxes; salutations to the Bestower of Boons upon Puṇḍalīka; salutations to the Supreme Ancient One; salutations to Affection; salutations to the One with the Eye on the Forehead; salutations to Bhairavī; salutations to the Giver of Prosperity; salutations to Bhrāmari.

Salutations to Bhramā; salutations to her whose nature is the three worlds—Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ; salutations to Māyā; salutations to Mṛgākṣī (the deer-eyed one); salutations to Mohahaṃtrī (the destroyer of delusion); salutations to Manasvinī; salutations to the bestower of great desires; salutations to her who removes the pride of mere measure; salutations to Madirekṣaṇā (the intoxicating-eyed one); salutations to Yuddhajñā (the knower of battle); salutations to Yaduvaṃśajā (born of the Yadu lineage); salutations to Yādavārtiharā (the remover of the distress of the Yādavas); salutations to the disciplined one; salutations to Yakṣiṇī; salutations to Yavanārdinī (the subduer of the Yavanas); salutations to Lakṣmī; salutations to Lāvaṇyarūpā (whose form is beauty); salutations to Lalitā.

Salutations to Lolalocanā; salutations to Līlāvatī; salutations to Lakṣarūpā; salutations to Vimalā; salutations to Vasu; salutations to Vyālarūpā; salutations to Vaidyavidyā; salutations to Vāsiṣṭhī; salutations to Vīryadāyinī; salutations to Śabalā; salutations to Śāntā; salutations to Śaktā; salutations to Śokavināśinī; salutations to Śatrumārī; salutations to Śatrurūpā; salutations to Sarasvatī; salutations to Suśroṇī; salutations to Sumukhī; salutations to Hāvabhūmi; salutations to Hāsyapriyā. Om. 6. The Garland of Names of Śrī Vijayalakṣmī.

Oṃ klīṃ oṃ, salutation to Vijayalakṣmī; salutation to Ambikā; salutation to Ambālikā; salutation to Ambudhiśayanā; salutation to Ambudhi; salutation to Antakaghnī; salutation to Antakartrī; salutation to Antimā; salutation to Antakarūpiṇī; salutation to Īḍyā; salutation to Ibhāsyanutā; salutation to Īśānapriyā; salutation to Ūti; salutation to Udyadbhānukoṭiprabhā; salutation to Udārāṅgā; salutation to Keliparā; salutation to Kalahā; salutation to Kāntalocanā; salutation to Kāñcī.

Salutations to Kanakadhārā; salutations to Kalyā; salutations to Kanakakuṇḍalā; salutations to Khaḍgahastā; salutations to Khaṭvāṅgavaradhāriṇī; salutations to Kheṭahastā; salutations to Gandhapriyā; salutations to Gopasakhī; salutations to Gāruḍī; salutations to Gatī; salutations to Go-hitā; salutations to Gopyā; salutations to Cit-ātmikā; salutations to Caturvargaphalapradā; salutations to Caturākṛti; salutations to Cakorākṣī; salutations to Cāruhāsā.

Salutations to the upholder of Govardhana; salutations to the venerable one; salutations to the bestower of fearlessness upon Gokula; salutations to her who is endowed with austerity; salutations to her who is worshipped by the assembly of ascetics; salutations to the remover of distress; salutations to the mother of Tārkṣya; salutations to Jaya; salutations to Japyā; salutations to Jarāyu; salutations to the swift one; salutations to the Mother; salutations to her adorned with gold; salutations to the treasury of compassion; salutations to Jvālā; salutations to her intent on the slaying of Jambha; salutations to the destroyer of suffering; salutations to the self-controlled one.

Salutations to Druteṣṭadā (the swift bestower of desires), salutations to Dātrī (the giver), salutations to Dīnartiśamanā (the pacifier of the suffering of the wretched), salutations to Nīlā (the blue one), salutations to Nāgendrapūjitā (worshipped by the lord of serpents), salutations to Nārasimhī (the lioness-like goddess), salutations to Nandinandā (the delighter of Nandin), salutations to Nandyāvartapriyā (fond of the *nandyāvarta* flower), salutations to Nidhi (the treasure), salutations to Paramānandā (supreme bliss), salutations to Padmahastā (lotus-handed), salutations to Pikasvarā (having the voice of a cuckoo), salutations to Puruṣārthapradā (bestower of the goals of human life), salutations to Prauḍhā (the mature/eloquent one), salutations to Prāpti (attainment), salutations to Balisamstutā (praised by Bali), salutations to Bālenduśekharā (crowned with the crescent moon), salutations to Bandyā (the one to be praised).

Salutations to the destroyer of child-seizing spirits; salutations to Brāhmī; salutations to Bṛhattamā; salutations to Bāṇā; salutations to Brāhmaṇī; salutations to Madhusravā; salutations to Mati; salutations to Medhā; salutations to Manīṣā; salutations to Mṛtyumārikā; salutations to Mṛgatvacī; salutations to the one beloved by yogis; salutations to the one whose nature is meditation on the limbs of yoga; salutations to Yajñabhū; salutations to Yajñavardhinī; salutations to Rākā; salutations to the one with a face like the full moon; salutations to Ramyā; salutations to the one with tinkling anklets.

Salutations to the slayer of demons; salutations to the giver of delight; salutations to the creeper; salutations to Līlā; salutations to her who has the form of a playful man; salutations to the restless one; salutations to the most excellent; salutations to the earth; salutations to the heroine; salutations to the most eminent; salutations to her who consists of gold; salutations to the Power (Śakti); salutations to the dark-complexioned one; salutations to the virtuous one; salutations to Śivā; salutations to Horā; salutations to her who rides upon horses. Om. 7. The Garland of Names of Śrī Vidyā-Lakṣmī.
Aiṃ Oṃ.

Salutations to Vidyālakṣmī; salutations to Vāgdevī; salutations to Paradevī; salutations to Niravadyā; salutations to Pustakahastā; salutations to Jñānamudrā; salutations to Śrīvidyā; salutations to Vidyārūpā; salutations to Śāstranirūpiṇī; salutations to Trikālajñānā; salutations to Sarasvatī; salutations to Mahāvidyā; salutations to Vāṇiśrī; salutations to Yaśasvinī; salutations to Vijayā; salutations to Akṣarā; salutations to Varṇā; salutations to Parāvidyā; salutations to Kavitā.

Salutations to the eternally awakened; salutations to the non-conceptual; salutations to her who transcends the Vedas; salutations to her whose form is beyond qualities; salutations to her whose form is partless; salutations to the stainless; salutations to her whose form is stainless; salutations to the formless; salutations to the changeless; salutations to the eternally pure; salutations to the intellect; salutations to liberation; salutations to the eternal; salutations to her who is free from ego; salutations to her who is free from affliction; salutations to the blemishless; salutations to her who is free from action; salutations to the cause of all.

Salutation to Mahālakṣmī. Oṃ. Now begins the *Śrī Kṣipraphalaprada Dhanalakṣmī Stotra*. Salutations to you who are the embodiment of all, salutations to the bestower of auspiciousness! O Goddess, granter of great prosperity, salutations to you, the giver of wealth. O Goddess, bestower of great enjoyment, fulfiller of great desires, O Goddess, giver of happiness and liberation, salutations to you, the giver of wealth. O you whose form is Brahman, eternal bliss, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss; O Goddess, bestower of attained perfections, salutations to you, the giver of wealth.

O Goddess who possesses the radiance of the rising sun, within the orb of the rising Aditya; O Goddess who bestows the essence of Śiva, salutations to you, the Giver of Wealth! O you whose form is Śiva, whose bliss is Śiva, whose body is the bliss of the Cause; O you whose form is the dissolution of the universe, salutations to you, the Giver of Wealth! O you whose nature is the five principles (*pañcatattva*), who are ever devoted to the fivefold conduct (*pañcācāra*); O Goddess who grants the desires of practitioners (*sādhaka*), salutations to you, the Giver of Wealth! Śrīṃ Oṃ. Oṃ Śrī Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī Parābhaṭṭārikā.
Salutations to the unified Śrī Candramaulīśvara Parabrahman. Victory, victory to Śaṅkara! Hara, Hara, Śaṅkara!
